scope: Supporting upstream design context for DUMMY-20H3 through DUMMY-20H6; not qualification authority by itself.

upstream.title: Reduce fixed abstractions in allocation during drought
summary: The issue identifies infeasibility when fixed abstractions would drive Basin storage negative.
It proposes reducing such fixed abstractions with a storage-dependent reduction factor.
The discussion explicitly notes concern that making reduction-factor behavior an optimization goal can produce unintuitive source releases.

upstream.title: Native multi objective optimization
summary: The PR states that issue #2323 is resolved by making the reduction factors goals after all.
The implementation uses lexicographic multi-objective optimization.
This supports interpreting low_storage_factor as an allocation decision variable/objective, not as a direct copy of the physical reduction factor.

research_relation: DUMMY-20H3 empirically showed current Basin infiltration enters the allocation problem as implicit negative forcing while the LP can choose low_storage_factor=0.
DUMMY-20H4 empirically separated physical low-storage factor=1 from LP low_storage_factor=0 on the same accepted state.
DUMMY-20H5 tests whether storage-preservation itself is sufficient to cause the LP factor collapse when LevelDemand machinery is removed.
DUMMY-20H6, if admitted after H5, tests the next-boundary asymmetry between accepted storage memory and current negative forcing.
interpretation_boundaries: Upstream history explains design intent but does not prove that any particular research observation is intended behavior.
Do not classify the observed coupling behavior as a defect from this context alone.
Product and research coupling conclusions remain evidence-driven by the preregistered DUMMY work units.
